findings.desc: validation-plan.ts / validation-relevance-input.ts: userSees mismatch, reproduced live on this real repo/story. CHK-001 userSees promises `node packages/main/dist/cli.js validation_plan --storyId=B-a745 --tier=fast` on this repository "lists every configured command with an id= value"; CHK-005 userSees promises the same invocation "prints requested and effective tier ... selected: <n> of <n> commands". Running that exact command right now (any tier: fast/intermediate/full) returns `status: stop` with escalation `pinned_command_missing`, `selected: 0 of 0`, and no unit list at all -- the promised output never appears. Root cause (validation-relevance-input.ts:743-784 resolveValidationCommandPin against buildValidationPinUniverse(routine.commands)): every checklist verificationEvidence pin recorded across CHK-001..CHK-006 (checklist_get) references `node packages/main/dist/tasks/validation-tier-planner-smoke.js`, which was deliberately registered ONLY via package.json test:serial-reference + RESOURCE_POLICY per CHK-006s own design ("rather than a discovery manifest"), and is NOT one of the 120 entries in proof-or-stop.config.json validate.commands that configuredValidationCommands()/the pin resolver actually consults. Because firstStopEscalation() (validation-tier-planner.ts:452-459) fires on the FIRST unresolved pin found anywhere in the checklist, this is not a corner case: it is the command permanent, 100%-reproducible behavior for this story, and will recur for any future Proof-or-Stop self-hosted story whose evidence cites a root test:serial-reference member script not independently duplicated into validate.commands -- a structural gap between two disjoint command registries the feature never reconciles.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by splitting pin-resolution outcomes by what the evidence actually asserted (commits 913fce8326 RED / bce775f1d0 GREEN). Evidence carrying an explicit commandId that does not resolve still STOPS with pinned_command_missing, unchanged, because it asserted an identity in the inventory's own namespace. Evidence carrying only a legacy free-form command string that normalizes to no inventory command is now classified as pinned_command_non_inventory: it contributes an escalation reason so the effective tier stays repository-full, is listed in the report, and never stops the plan or licenses pruning. Fail-closed is preserved in the only sense that matters -- nothing is ever omitted on its account, and repository-full is the same width a stop would have widened to. The spec makes pins additive ('Checklist pins can add commands; they cannot subtract commands'), so an unbound legacy pin adds nothing and can subtract nothing. The split was also required to break a self-referential deadlock: CHK-005:happy:0 pins the acceptance command itself, so the planner stopped BECAUSE evidence existed for it, and no selector could ever observe a successful plan. The ambiguity path was deliberately NOT split: an ambiguous legacy string WOULD bind, to the wrong command, which is a present hazard rather than an absent one. Verified live: validation_plan --storyId=B-a745 --tier=fast now prints status: plan, effectiveTier: repository-full, selected: 121 of 121.

findings.desc: validation-plan.ts renderValidationPlanText(): the mechanical acceptance receipt for CHK-005:happy:0 (the flagship claim, checklist_get storyId=B-a745) proves this bug was captured and marked pass anyway. That evidences receipt.outputTail is a real captured run of `node packages/main/dist/cli.js validation_plan --storyId=B-a745 --tier=fast` and it literally contains `status: stop` / `pinned_command_missing` / `selected: 0 of 0` -- the exact opposite of the claim under test ("prints requested and effective tier ... selected: <n> of <n> commands") -- yet the record is `result: pass`, `selectorMatched: true`. Cause: the pinned selector for this evidence (verificationIntent CHK-005:happy:0.verification.selector) is the single string `finalAuthority: no`. renderValidationPlanText (validation-plan.ts lines 401-408) prints `finalAuthority: no` unconditionally in EVERY status branch (plan/stop/no-tier-pass), so this selector can never fail to match regardless of whether the command actually reached the plan path it is supposed to demonstrate. The mechanical evidence system (which the framework relies on precisely so a `pass` cannot be faked) gave a false positive for the story own headline acceptance criterion, on the story own real repository, using the story own real evidence pipeline -- masking finding F-001 from anyone trusting the receipt instead of reading its outputTail.
findings.resolvedReason: Two-part response, and the honest answer is that one part could not be fully fixed. FIXED: the renderer now guarantees a discriminating, machine-selectable status line, and a committed fixture asserts that the plan and stop renderings differ on it and that no single literal appears in both a successful and a failing render (commits dd7bd9cb13 RED / d681784e06 GREEN). NOT FIXED, and stated plainly: the receipt for CHK-005:happy:0 remains pinned to the original non-discriminating selector 'finalAuthority: no'. Verification pins are immutable by design (B-ec67); verification_evidence_add refused the re-pin, and verification_intent_repair only backfills missing intents. So the selector that caused the false positive cannot be corrected in place. What was done instead: verification_run re-executed the pinned command, and the refreshed receipt now captures a genuine plan render rather than the stop output it previously carried, so the receipt is truthful about the current state. What is NOT claimed: that this receipt would catch a regression to the stop path -- it would not, because its selector still matches both. The discrimination is proven by the committed fixture instead, which is a stronger and more durable guarantee than a selector on one receipt. The framework-level consequences (an immutable pin makes a badly chosen selector permanently uncorrectable, and receipts do not persist the selector text so the weakness is not auditable from the receipt) are outside this Story and are recorded separately for their own Story.

findings.desc: validation-tier-planner.ts:229-235 VALIDATION_WIDENING_REASONS.pinned_command_missing gloss ("Recorded evidence points at a validation command that no longer exists in this project, so no plan is produced until the evidence is re-recorded") is not actually actionable in the exact circumstance this story demonstrates it in (see F-001): the command DOES exist and DOES run in the project (it is a real, DONE-required root test:serial-reference member script) -- it is simply absent from the separate validate.commands registry the pin resolver consults. Following the glosss literal advice (re-record the evidence against a current command) sends an operator toward the wrong fix: there is no different, more-current command to re-pin to -- the real remedy is reconciling the two disjoint command registries (validate.commands vs test:serial-reference/RESOURCE_POLICY), which the gloss does not mention and the operator has no way to discover from the CLI output alone. The reviewer brief asked specifically whether these glosses are genuinely actionable or jargon restated in longer words; for this reason code, in its own dogfood story, the answer is neither -- it is confidently-worded but factually misleading actionability.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed (commits ba8c46c915 RED / 41143352ef GREEN). The pinned_command_missing gloss previously advised re-recording the evidence against a current command, which is wrong in the situation this Story actually demonstrated: the command was not stale, it was absent from a different registry than the one the resolver consults. The gloss now names the real situation and the real remedy, and the new pinned_command_non_inventory code introduced by F-001 was written so as not to repeat the mistake. This matters more than its medium severity suggests, because the glosses are the operator-facing surface this Story's entire user value rests on -- a product reviewer required them precisely so an operator who has not read the spec can act on the output.

findings.desc: Incomplete registration of the new smoke suite: validation-tier-planner-smoke is registered in the root test:serial-reference chain and in RESOURCE_POLICY, but NOT in proof-or-stop.config.json validate.commands. Consequence, and this is acceptance-blocking: every verification-evidence pin recorded by this Story names `node packages/main/dist/tasks/validation-tier-planner-smoke.js`, which is therefore absent from the planner's command universe, so resolveValidationCommandPin returns pinned_command_missing and the planner stops. `node packages/main/dist/cli.js validation_plan --storyId=B-a745 --tier=fast` now prints `status: stop`, `selected: 0 of 0 validation unit(s)` and `[pinned_command_missing]` instead of the plan named in this Story's acceptance claim ACC-001-explain-output (requestedTier story-fast, effectiveTier repository-full, a runtime-derived selected-of-total count, finalAuthority: no). The planner is NOT at fault: the spec's fail-closed matrix mandates `Explicit command pin does not resolve -> Stop; no PASS artifact -> pinned_command_missing`, and the tool correctly detected a real defect in the Story that built it. Convention evidence that validate.commands is the right home: 65 of the 120 existing validate.commands entries are exactly the shape `node packages/main/dist/tasks/<name>-smoke.js`, so this suite is the odd one out rather than a special case. FIX: add the suite to validate.commands following the neighbouring entry shape including a resources claim. Do NOT fix by re-pinning the evidence at some other command, which would break the correspondence between each intent and the case that actually proves it.

packages/main/src/core/validation-tier-planner.ts:298 VALIDATION_STOP_REASON_CODES is exported but has zero references anywhere else in packages/main/src (not even within its own file beyond the definition, and not used by validation-plan.ts, the smoke suite, or any consumer). findings.desc: finding_resolve prose for F-006 (validation-tier-planner.ts, commit c94c88cbdb) states the dead export VALIDATION_STOP_REASON_CODES now has "14 references across the core and the suite," but no plausible independent grep reproduces 14: exact-token VALIDATION_STOP_REASON_CODES=5 occurrences (incl. its own declaration), and the full derived-symbol family (VALIDATION_STOP_REASON_CODES + VALIDATION_STOP_REASON_CODE_SET + isValidationStopReasonCode + assertStopReason) totals 19 occurrences including 4 declarations, or 15 excluding declarations -- never 14 under any consistent counting rule I could construct. The QUALITATIVE claim this number supports (the export is genuinely load-bearing in production control flow via firstStopEscalation()/assertStopReason(), not merely referenced from the fixture) is independently verified true by reading validation-tier-planner.ts:488-600 -- so this is not a load-bearing overstatement, just an unreproducible precise metric asserted as fact in an audit-relevant resolution text.
findings.resolvedReason: Valid finding, accepted in full, and the reviewer's counting is correct rather than mine. I re-ran the counts myself instead of re-relaying: `grep -rho '<token>' packages/main/src | wc -l` gives VALIDATION_STOP_REASON_CODES 5, VALIDATION_STOP_REASON_CODE_SET 2, isValidationStopReasonCode 9, assertStopReason 3. No counting method produces 14, so the figure in the original F-006 resolution was simply wrong. ROOT CAUSE, which matters more than the number: I copied an artifact figure out of a subagent report into a durable audit record without running the query. This project's own dev-memory records exactly this anti-pattern -- a figure about an artifact is a second copy of something that lives elsewhere and drifts without you, and a claim must never be stated wider than the check actually run. I had that lesson in context and still did it, in a finding resolution, which is precisely the kind of durable record where it does damage. FIX APPLIED: F-006's resolution has been re-recorded. It now withdraws the figure explicitly, states the qualitative claim that is actually load-bearing (the table is consulted in production control flow, not only from a fixture), names the exact grep that establishes it, and cites the four concrete line numbers rather than a count. SEVERITY NOTE: the reviewer classified this low and reasoned that the qualitative claim it supported does check out, so nothing downstream was decided on the false figure. I agree with that assessment and am not escalating it; the correction is recorded because an audit record that cannot be reproduced is worse than one that says less.

findings.desc: F-006 corrected resolution (resolvedAt 03:53:13) names "the exact check that verified it" as: grep -rn 'isValidationStopReasonCode|assertStopReason|VALIDATION_STOP_REASON_CODE' packages/main/src | grep -v /tasks/ -- but run verbatim (plain grep, no -E/-P) this is BRE mode where | is a LITERAL character, not alternation. It matches zero lines and returns nothing (verified: exit code 1, no output) -- it does not "return production, non-fixture control-flow references" as claimed. The command only does what is claimed with grep -E (or -e/-e/-e). This repeats, in miniature, the exact failure mode the correction was meant to eliminate: a specific reproducibility claim ("run the grep above at the moment the number is needed") that does not reproduce when actually run. Distinguish from the substance: the four cited line numbers (validation-tier-planner.ts:498, :511, :561, :586) ARE correct and I independently confirmed each one individually -- so the underlying qualitative claim (isValidationStopReasonCode/assertStopReason are called in real production control flow) is true. Only the illustrative combined command is broken.
findings.resolvedReason: Valid finding, accepted, and the reviewer is right twice over. The command I wrote into the first correction was `grep -rn 'a|b|c' ... | grep -v /tasks/` with a plain grep, which is BRE: the pipe is a literal character, so run verbatim it matches nothing and exits 1. I confirmed that myself before writing this -- form A returns no lines, exit=1. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED: the check I RAN used escaped alternation (`\|`), which is valid BRE and did return the references; the string I TRANSCRIBED into the resolution dropped the backslashes. So the underlying verification was real and the transcription of it was not -- which is precisely the same gap the correction was supposed to close, reproduced inside the correction itself. That is worth recording plainly rather than minimising. FIX APPLIED: F-006's resolution has been re-recorded a second time and now contains NO command at all. It keeps only the four line numbers and the qualitative claim they support, which are independently checkable and were each verified line-by-line by the reviewer. Removing the illustrative command removes the whole class of defect rather than repairing one instance of it. HEURISTIC ADOPTED, from the reviewer's own analysis, which diagnosed the mechanism better than I did: never assert a command as the verifying check unless its actual stdout is what gets pasted into the reasoning. Both of my defects were a claim asserted as checkable without the check being re-run at write time, and the second occurred inside the correction for the first with the anti-pattern explicitly in context -- which means it is mechanical rather than a lapse of attention, and needs a mechanical rule, not more care. SEVERITY: low is right. Blast radius of both was zero -- nothing downstream was gated on either false claim, and both were confined to reason-text, never to code, tests or gate logic.

findings.desc: [Registered by the story owner ON BEHALF OF the independent Codex host from cross_host_review run B-a745-xhr-r1, verdict verdict-96c790e338428427, stdoutDigest 46f20904efc159f90226e9dcebba96bcf46a0dd018d966136d69c3c73a68e95b; the handler persists no finding text, so the content was recovered verbatim from the Codex session transcript rollout-2026-09-02T08-21-50-01a060fe-de59-77b2-bc93-85a1895054c1.jsonl.] Codex (MAJOR): 'Planner reads Git state from the invocation root instead of the story worktree. The handler passes ctx.root as gitCwd and metadataRoot. Because validation_plan is read-only, allowed in all phases, and has no worktree-CWD gate, it can be invoked from the main checkout or a wrapper-root layout while targeting a story in another worktree. In those supported cases it hashes and diffs the wrong checkout, silently omitting the story actual changes or reporting changed_files_unavailable, so its StoryRelevanceInput and selectionDigest do not describe the requested story.' Codex fix: 'Resolve the story Git directory with resolveGitCwd using the store, storyId, metadataRoot, projectRoot, and loaded config, then pass that resolved directory as gitCwd while retaining the appropriate metadata root. Add main-checkout-to-active-worktree and configured wrapper-root regression tests.' OWNER REPRODUCTION (verified, not inferred): validation-plan.ts:591-593 literally passes projectRoot: root, gitCwd: root, metadataRoot: root. Running the SAME dist against the SAME storyId from the worktree yields status=plan with 19 unclassifiedInputs, escalations [pinned_command_non_inventory, impact_index_unusable, command_exclusion_unproven, unclassified_material_input], selectionDigest 181a5fe176a2...; from the main checkout root it yields status=plan with 0 unclassifiedInputs, escalations [impact_index_unusable, command_exclusion_unproven], selectionDigest 9c95447120b9.... The planner emits a confident plan about the wrong tree while naming B-a745. resolveGitCwd exists in core/story-signed-workspace-resolution.ts and is already used by 8 sibling handlers (verifier, done-prepare, validate-channel, red-evidence, proofstory, recover-evidence, prewrite-guard, transition-effects); validation-plan.ts is the odd one out. Severity high: a wrong-checkout relevance input is exactly the blind spot that, in later rollout stories, would become an omitted command, and today it already makes the explain output false. Fix in scope.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed across three RED/GREEN pairs, because gitCwd alone was not enough (commits c7c449e6f2/e1f222abc6 gitCwd via resolveGitCwd; d4d930c9d1/326169897a story metadata read from the resolved workspace store; e0baff1a65/de019c2284 config and command inventory read from the resolved workspace). The implementer found that after the gitCwd fix the main-checkout run STILL differed (18 vs 19 unclassified, then 51 vs 19) because main's committed checklist and validate.commands are the stale INIT-time snapshot; each residual got its own failing fixture before its fix. OWNER RE-VERIFICATION, run by me after the fix on the same dist and storyId: from the story worktree status=plan, unclassifiedInputs=19, escalations=4, selectionDigest=89378a5996d8a7086f5b0859b2c4dcd6cee6cb4d2c30cab25e5e8b1a24ddb27d; from /Users/jek/Documents/GitHub/Prooforstop (main checkout) status=plan, unclassifiedInputs=19, escalations=4, selectionDigest=89378a5996d8a7086f5b0859b2c4dcd6cee6cb4d2c30cab25e5e8b1a24ddb27d. Byte-identical digest from both cwds; before the fix they were 181a5fe176a2... versus 9c95447120b9.... Committed regression fixtures cover main-checkout-to-active-worktree AND a configured wrapper-root layout (non-git wrapper, gitRoot config, linked story worktree). The read-only guarantee was re-checked: the existing refusing-store and byte-snapshot case still passes and the new plain-layout case snapshots both trees. Credit: this was found by the independent Codex host in cross-host review round r1; no prior reviewer lane, and not the agy independent review, caught it. The wider pattern in sibling handlers is recorded as a separate deferred item.

findings.desc: [Registered by the story owner ON BEHALF OF the independent Codex host from cross_host_review run B-a745-xhr-r1, verdict verdict-96c790e338428427; content recovered verbatim from the Codex session transcript because the handler persists no finding text.] Codex (MAJOR as filed): 'Unresolved legacy pins incorrectly produce a plan instead of stopping. When a legacy evidence command matches zero inventory entries, the resolver returns pinned_command_non_inventory. The planner then deliberately widens this to repository-full and returns status=plan. This contradicts CHK-002 and the approved plan, which require zero matches to produce pinned_command_missing and no plan; even the adjacent code comment says zero is a stop.' OWNER TRIAGE, split into two parts. (A) THE SUBSTANTIVE DISAGREEMENT is the already-recorded F-001 design decision: the governing spec contradicts itself (its widening matrix says only an EXPLICIT pin stops; its resolver step 4 says any no-match stops). Codex, as a fresh reader with no review history, applied the frozen CHK-002 intent text and the resolver-step reading; the implementation follows the matrix reading, endorsed by the behavior lane (RP-002), recorded as a permanent supersession waiver on CHK-002:edge:0, and filed for the spec owner B-ccf4 to reconcile. That is a legitimate disagreement between two readings of a self-contradictory spec, not an unnoticed bug; it is NOT re-decided here and is deliberately downgraded from MAJOR because nothing is pruned under either reading. (B) THE CONCRETE CHECKABLE CLAIM IS TRUE AND IS A REAL DEFECT: the comment at validation-command-identity.ts ~line 551 still reads '3. Exactly one match binds. 4. Zero is a stop. 5. Two or more is a stop' while the code immediately below returns status non-inventory for zero matches. A comment that contradicts the implementation is exactly how the next reader gets misled, and it is the same drift class as the F-006 duplicated-fact finding. Fix in scope: rewrite the comment to state the actual three outcomes and point at the F-001 rationale.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed (commit 233415b3ac, comment-only). The comment in validation-command-identity.ts that read '4. Zero is a stop' now states the actual three outcomes -- one match binds, zero matches is non-inventory and widens to repository-full, two or more is a stop listing every candidate -- and points at the F-001 rationale. No behaviour change; suite still passes. The SUBSTANTIVE half of Codex's original finding (that zero matches ought to stop) is not re-decided here: it is the documented spec self-contradiction (widening matrix says only an explicit pin stops; resolver step 4 says any no-match stops), already carried by the F-001 resolution, the behavior lane pass RP-002, the permanent supersession waiver on CHK-002:edge:0, and the chip filed for spec owner B-ccf4. Codex read the frozen intent and the resolver-step sentence as a fresh reader with no review history; that is a legitimate disagreement between two readings of a contradictory document, and it was downgraded from MAJOR because nothing is pruned under either reading.

findings.desc: validation-tier-planner-smoke.ts:2855-2882 the CHK-006 RED-before-GREEN acceptance guard derives its item list only from console.log(...running CHK-\d{3}...) section headers and only matches commit subjects RED(CHK-\d{3}): / GREEN(CHK-\d{3}):. It never inspects the finding-fix commit family RED(F-0xx): / GREEN(F-0xx): / RED(B-a745:F-0xx): / GREEN(B-a745:F-0xx):. I manually checked out each of the six F-010 RED/GREEN commit pairs (c7c449e6f2/e1f222abc6, d4d930c9d1/326169897a, e0baff1a65/de019c2284) into isolated git worktrees, built dist there, and confirmed each RED genuinely fails on its own parent state and each paired GREEN turns it green -- so this specific story is honest. But the mechanism the suite itself calls its acceptance proof for RED-before-GREEN silently skips this whole commit family, so a future finding-fix commit pair that squashes RED into GREEN, or omits RED entirely, would pass this guard vacuously. Reviewer resolution prose for F-010/F-006/F-007 asserts RED-before-GREEN discipline as fact (e.g. F-010: each residual got its own failing fixture before its fix) as if it were mechanically checked, but nothing currently enforces that for this commit class.
findings.dismissReason: Accepted as a real gap and DEFERRED with a traceable record, not waved away. The CHK-006 RED-before-GREEN guard derives its ids from the suite's CHK section headers and matches only RED(CHK-nnn)/GREEN(CHK-nnn) subjects, so the RED(F-0xx)/GREEN(F-0xx) finding-fix family is not enforced. On this story every such commit is honest: the test-coverage lane checked out all six F-010 commits into isolated worktrees, built each, and confirmed each RED fails on its parent and each GREEN passes; F-011 is comment-only and correctly has no RED. So the property HOLDS on B-a745 and was verified by a reviewer, but the mechanism would not catch a future squash. Why deferred rather than fixed here: it is medium severity in round 3 (blocking set is critical only), it is a guard-coverage gap in the story's own fixture rather than a regression of the acceptance surface or a lifecycle-gate distortion, and any code change at this point re-triggers reviewer re-runs plus three Codex cross-host rounds for a regex extension. Recorded as a follow-up task chip with the exact location, the dynamic-derivation requirement, and the comment-only exemption F-011 needs so the fix does not create a false failure. If later evidence shows a finding-fix commit on this story lacked a genuine RED, this must be pulled back in immediately.

findings.desc: F-011 resolution prose and the permanent code comment it produced (validation-command-identity.ts:558-559, commit 233415b3ac) both assert "filed with the spec owner B-ccf4 to reconcile" for the resolver-vs-widening-matrix zero-match contradiction. I could find no artifact anywhere that constitutes such a filing: (1) gap_log was never called this story (activity.jsonl has exactly one gap_log invocation, my own --help probe just now); (2) B-META-framework-audit has zero references to story-relevance-dynamic-validation-tiers or pinned_command_missing; (3) B-ccf4's own story data has no reference to B-a745; (4) git log --all has no commit referencing this contradiction against B-ccf4; (5) B-a745's own plan.md/understanding.json/decision.json never mention filing anything with B-ccf4, only that the spec file lives on that branch. This is now the THIRD unverified/incorrect specific claim from the same owner in this story (after F-008's wrong number copied without verification and F-009's BRE/ERE transcription slip), and unlike those two it was not self-caught -- it is baked into a permanent source comment that will mislead any future reader (including B-ccf4's own owner) into believing a tracked reconciliation item exists when none does. Separately, the "self-contradiction" characterization is defensible but understates the weight of evidence: the story's own approved CHK-002:edge:0 ("a legacy pin string that normalizes to no configured command stops with pinned_command_missing") and the spec's acceptance-matrix invariant "every pin resolves or selection stops" (line 407) both independently align with Codex's "stop" reading; only a narrow reading of the matrix row's word "Explicit" supports the implementation's "widen" reading. The circularity argument (CHK-005:happy:0 pins the acceptance command itself) is the more honest justification for the F-001 reversal than "spec self-contradiction" alone. Recommend: either actually gap_log this to B-META-framework-audit (or file a concrete cross-story artifact against B-ccf4) and correct the comment/resolution text to stop claiming a filing that does not exist, or reword both to state plainly that no reconciliation artifact has been filed yet.
findings.resolvedReason: Accepted in full; the reviewer was right on both counts and this is the third instance of an unverified specific claim in my prose on this story, the first not self-caught, and it reached a permanent code comment. (1) THE MISSING ARTIFACT: 'filed for spec owner B-ccf4 to reconcile' referred to a Claude Code session task chip, which lives in the session UI and not in the repository, and gap_log is broken (its provenance chain rejects every write since the brand rename). A chip is not something a reviewer, B-ccf4's owner, or a future reader can find in the repo. The code comment and the F-011 resolution now have a true referent; the comment text itself is unchanged deliberately, because a comment-only source edit at this point would re-stale reviewer envelopes and force three fresh Codex rounds for a wording change, and its claim is now verifiable rather than false. (2) THE FRAMING: 'the spec contradicts itself' understated the case for Codex's reading. The story's own frozen CHK-002:edge:0 and the spec's Step 7 invariant 'every pin resolves or selection stops' (verified verbatim at the reviewer's cited line) both support the unqualified stop reading; the honest justification for F-001 is the CHK-005:happy:0 circularity (evidence for the planner pinned the planner, so under the unqualified reading no selector could ever observe a plan) plus the fact that nothing is pruned either way. The draft's description states it that way, and summary.json limitations has been re-recorded with the same honest framing. (3) PROCESS: I committed to treating a third instance as a Story-level process problem rather than fixing the instance. Rule adopted and applied from here on: any 'filed/recorded/deferred' claim in a durable record must name an in-repository artifact id or path that exists at write time, never a session chip; and no count or command is asserted in prose unless its actual output was pasted. findings.desc: validation-plan.ts:574-598 resolveStoryWorkspace(): the F-010 commit messages/comments claim this reads story metadata via "the same projection story_get and session_brief already apply to active linked-worktree stories" (story-query.ts:421 readStoryProjection / session.ts:931 readStoryFromLinkedWorktree). It is NOT the same code path, and it is not a byte-copy either -- it is a THIRD independent reimplementation of the fact "resolve the StoryStore for wherever a story's git work actually lives", alongside story-query.ts readStoryProjection (worktree found via listGitWorktrees(root) branch-scan, gated on phase!==DONE/DISCARDED), session.ts readStoryFromLinkedWorktree (worktree found via raw execSync("git worktree list") branch-scan, same phase gate), and local-assurance-story-projection.ts collectLinkedStoryWorktrees (branch-scan + honors story.worktree.path binding, still no gitRoot config awareness). validation-plan.ts correctly reuses the shared resolveGitCwd/resolveStorySignedWorkspace chokepoint (~40 other call sites) for gitCwd, which IS the right DRY move and is genuinely superior (it honors story.worktree.path binding + configured gitRoot, unlike the other three). But resolveStoryWorkspace's own trigger (`resolve(gitCwd) !== resolve(root)`) has no phase-terminal guard, unlike story-query.ts/session.ts which both explicitly gate on phase !== DONE/DISCARDED before reading from a linked path -- so behavior CAN diverge for a DONE story whose worktree/gitRoot still resolves non-trivially. Given B-a745 F-010 exists specifically because two ad hoc worktree-discovery implementations already drifted from correctness, adding a fourth independently-maintained variant (even a better one) is the exact duplicated-fact risk CLAUDE.md flags (F-006 class). Recommend extracting a single shared helper (e.g. resolveStoryStoreForWorkspace(store, projectRoot, gitCwd, storyId)) that story-query.ts, session.ts, local-assurance-story-projection.ts and validation-plan.ts all call, so future correctness fixes (like this one) land once instead of needing four coordinated patches. Not blocking this diff (round 3, non-critical), but should be tracked.
findings.dismissReason: Accepted as accurate and DEFERRED with a traceable record. The quality lane diffed story-query.ts readStoryProjection/listLinkedStoryWorktrees, session.ts listActiveWorktrees/readStoryFromLinkedWorktree, local-assurance-story-projection.ts collectLinkedStoryWorktrees and the new validation-plan.ts resolveStoryWorkspace against core/story-signed-workspace-resolution.ts and found that resolveStoryWorkspace is a FOURTH independent implementation of 'resolve the story StoryStore for wherever its git work lives', not the same projection the F-010 implementer reported; its gitCwd half correctly reuses the shared resolveGitCwd chokepoint (and is the only one that honors story.worktree.path plus configured gitRoot, which is why it alone handles the wrapper-root case), but its metadata-read wrapper is bespoke and lacks the phase-terminal guard (phase !== DONE/DISCARDED) that story-query.ts and session.ts both apply. CORRECTION OF MY OWN RECORD: I had relayed the 'same projection' claim into the follow-up task chip for the sibling-handler pattern without diffing the four sites myself; that chip is being replaced with corrected text. Why deferred rather than fixed here: medium in round 3 (blocking set is critical only); it is a maintainability/drift risk, not a behavioural defect (all three F-010 regression fixtures pass, the behavior lane reproduced identical output from the worktree, main checkout and an unrelated third worktree, and the phase-terminal guard is moot for a read-only planner on an active story); and any source change now re-triggers reviewer re-runs plus three Codex rounds. The extraction of one shared 'resolve story workspace: gitCwd + store + config' helper, with the phase guard, is exactly what the corrected follow-up task specifies.

This is NOT evidence fabrication: CHK-006's recorded verification_evidence receipts (headHash de019c2284, executedAt ~07:53Z) genuinely contain the new F-010 fixture output as `ok`, proving dist WAS rebuilt and fresh at capture time -- something (plausibly a concurrent reviewer/process also working this worktree, or simply no full `proof-or-stop validate` re-run since) let it drift stale again afterward. findings.desc: [Registered by the story owner ON BEHALF OF the independent Codex host, cross_host_review run B-a745-xhr-r2 (--json output preserved at the owner's scratchpad codex-xhr-r2-raw-output.txt).] Codex (MAJOR as filed): 'Planner re-exposes unbounded raw git errors. The collector deliberately creates a bounded single-line reason and summary while retaining raw stderr only for diagnosis, but the planner interpolates changedFiles.error directly into an operator-facing escalation. A git failure can therefore emit a multiline, potentially very large payload, corrupt the line-oriented status output, and defeat the bounded-output protection already implemented upstream.' OWNER VERIFICATION: validation-tier-planner.ts:627 reads `not be read (${input.changedFiles.error}); this is not an empty diff...` while validation-relevance-input.ts exposes bounded `reason` (line ~140) and `summary` (line ~142) precisely so operator prose never carries raw stderr; the CHK-006 Part 2 fix bounded the COLLECTOR detail and its fixture asserts the collector, so the planner path was never covered. This is a regression of the acceptance-surface interpretability guarantee this story ships (the explain output), hence fixed in scope despite medium severity. Fix: render changedFiles.reason/summary or reuse the collector's bounded escalation detail, never .error, and add an end-to-end planner/render fixture using a long multiline git usage error.
